comment.narrative: The process was cancelled due to operational context change and shifted priorities of the beneficiaries.Due to the invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation on 24 February 2022 an urgent need arose to provide emergency and resilience assistance to the Ukrainian authoritiesand the affected people. Thus the works that were initially planned in the Bridging project were completed to a limited extent. In close coordination with the EUD IOM shifted the focus of the project to contribute to responding to urgent needs of project beneficiaries and affected populations. In November 2022 Addendum 2 to the Contribution Agreement ENI424863 was signed to retroactively formalize all programmatic changes as well as to extend the project duration until the end of March 2023. This was done to enable the completion of the delivery of pending procurement items in a complex logistics and supply chains context ensure continued technical assistance for the project beneficiaries and compile key results produced through the original Bridging project to define key next priorities for IBM in Ukraine. Despite drastic changes in the security and programmaticoperational environment in February 2022 the project achieved the following full analysis of relevant business processes of the project beneficiaries two audits of project beneficiaries information and communications technology ICT infrastructure development of two ICT strategic vision documents development of two governance documents for project beneficiaries key information systems development of 41 legal reports one draft vision document development of one draft project plan and development of draft work packages in view of the EU4IBM2 project. After February 2022 the project responded to urgent and strategic needs of the project beneficiaries including support to their data security and ICT infrastructure procurement of medical kits and personal protective equipment. The assistance provided contributed to the Ukrainian government authorities safeguarding their vital operations and functions in the emergency situation. The project also supported internally displaced people IDPs in Zakarpattia region and the information campaign on the EU temporary protection directive reached more than 182000 individuals.

After February 2022 the project responded to urgent and strategic needs of the project beneficiaries including support to their data security and ICT infrastructure procurement of medical kits and personal protective equipment. The assistance provided contributed to the Ukrainian government authorities safeguarding their vital operations and functions in the emergency situation. The project also supported internally displaced people IDPs in Zakarpattia region and the information campaign on the EU temporary protection directive reached more than 182000 individuals.

comment.narrative: Enhancement finalization and approval of the Project Plan was cancelled due to change of the operational context and shifted priorities of the beneficiaries.Due to the invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation on 24 February 2022 an urgent need arose to provide emergency and resilience assistance to the Ukrainian authoritiesand the affected people. Thus the works that were initially planned in the Bridging project were completed to a limited extent. In close coordination with the EUD IOM shifted the focus of the project to contribute to responding to urgent needs of project beneficiaries and affected populations. In November 2022 Addendum 2 to the Contribution Agreement ENI424863 was signed to retroactively formalize all programmatic changes as well as to extend the project duration until the end of March 2023. This was done to enable the completion of the delivery of pending procurement items in a complex logistics and supply chains context ensure continued technical assistance for the project beneficiaries and compile key results produced through the original Bridging project to define key next priorities for IBM in Ukraine. Despite drastic changes in the security and programmaticoperational environment in February 2022 the project achieved the following full analysis of relevant business processes of the project beneficiaries two audits of project beneficiaries information and communications technology ICT infrastructure development of two ICT strategic vision documents development of two governance documents for project beneficiaries key information systems development of 41 legal reports one draft vision document development of one draft project plan and development of draft work packages in view of the EU4IBM2 project. After February 2022 the project responded to urgent and strategic needs of the project beneficiaries including support to their data security and ICT infrastructure procurement of medical kits and personal protective equipment. The assistance provided contributed to the Ukrainian government authorities safeguarding their vital operations and functions in the emergency situation. The project also supported internally displaced people IDPs in Zakarpattia region and the information campaign on the EU temporary protection directive reached more than 182000 individuals.

comment.narrative: With support from this project the beneficiaries reviewed and updated their strategic ICT visions so those could meet the EU and industry standards and best practices.Process was cancelled due to operational context change and shifted priorities of the beneficiaries.Due to the invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation on 24 February 2022 an urgent need arose to provide emergency and resilience assistance to the Ukrainian authoritiesand the affected people. Thus the works that were initially planned in the Bridging project were completed to a limited extent. In close coordination with the EUD IOM shifted the focus of the project to contribute to responding to urgent needs of project beneficiaries and affected populations. In November 2022 Addendum 2 to the Contribution Agreement ENI424863 was signed to retroactively formalize all programmatic changes as well as to extend the project duration until the end of March 2023. This was done to enable the completion of the delivery of pending procurement items in a complex logistics and supply chains context ensure continued technical assistance for the project beneficiaries and compile key results produced through the original Bridging project to define key next priorities for IBM in Ukraine. Despite drastic changes in the security and programmaticoperational environment in February 2022 the project achieved the following full analysis of relevant business processes of the project beneficiaries two audits of project beneficiaries information and communications technology ICT infrastructure development of two ICT strategic vision documents development of two governance documents for project beneficiaries key information systems development of 41 legal reports one draft vision document development of one draft project plan and development of draft work packages in view of the EU4IBM2 project. After February 2022 the project responded to urgent and strategic needs of the project beneficiaries including support to their data security and ICT infrastructure procurement of medical kits and personal protective equipment. The assistance provided contributed to the Ukrainian government authorities safeguarding their vital operations and functions in the emergency situation. The project also supported internally displaced people IDPs in Zakarpattia region and the information campaign on the EU temporary protection directive reached more than 182000 individuals.
